description: Given Dagster Slack notifications — SlackResource, make_slack_on_run_failure_sensor, or op success/failure hooks — determine whether the message is a run-status notification (pipeline- or task-scoped Orchestra alerts: block, destination not connection_id) or an explicit mid-run pipeline step (SLACK integration task with SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE), and author the corresponding YAML.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster Slack failure notification to an Orchestra pipeline-level alert (see files/slack_run_failure_sensor.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A pipeline-level alerts: entry firing on FAILED with a single SLACK destination (destination: '#eng-oncall', no connection_id field) — the literal channel carried straight through since only the bot token, not the channel, is environment-dependent.

assertions.text: The SLACK destination sets destination (SLACK/EMAIL require destination, not connection_id)
The #eng-oncall channel is carried over as the SLACK destination value
connection_id is NOT set on the SLACK destination — Slack alerts resolve from the workspace Slack connection; connection_id is only required for PAGER_DUTY/TEAMS/WEBHOOK/DATADOG
The channel is placed directly as the literal string '#eng-oncall' rather than routed through ${{ ENV.* }}, since the source only reads the bot token — not the channel — from an environment variable

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster op-level Slack success hook to an Orchestra task-level alert on the load_warehouse task only — it should not fire for the whole pipeline (see files/slack_success_hook_op.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A task-level alerts: entry on the load-warehouse task (not the pipeline root) firing on SUCCEEDED with a SLACK destination (destination: '#warehouse-notifications', no connection_id field), since an op-scoped hook maps to a task-level alert, not a job-wide sensor.

assertions.text: Output is a valid YAML document
The SLACK destination sets destination (SLACK/EMAIL require destination, not connection_id)
The #warehouse-notifications channel is carried over as the SLACK destination value
The alert is placed on the load-warehouse TaskModel (task-level), not the pipeline root alerts: block — matching the op-scoped @success_hook rather than a job-wide run-status sensor
extract_data, which has no hook, does not also get this alert

evals.prompt: This Dagster job posts a Slack message mid-run, after the dbt build finishes and before the downstream load starts (see files/slack_mid_pipeline_message.py). Convert this to the appropriate Orchestra pipeline construct — this is a workflow step, not a status notification. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live sends, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A SLACK pipeline task (integration: SLACK, integration_job: SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE) with parameters.channel_name '#data-team' and text set, wired via depends_on so it runs after the run_dbt_build task and before load_downstream — NOT an alerts: block, since this is an explicit step whose position in the run matters.

assertions.text: Output is a valid YAML document
A SLACK integration task is present
The task sets a channel_name parameter
The #data-team channel is carried over as the channel_name value
This is expressed as a SLACK/SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE task wired via depends_on, not an alerts: block, since the message is a positioned mid-run step rather than a run-status notification
The task's depends_on reflects it firing after the dbt build task and before the downstream load task, preserving the source's execution order
